title.narrative: Swedish Chemicals Agency: Ukraine project design support 2023-2024

description.narrative: Kemikalieinspektionen har inkommit med en ansökan om en projektförberedande insats i Ukraina. Miljöministeriet i Ukraina har efterfrågat svensk stöd rörande reformer och EU-anpassning inom miljöområdet. Detta projekt syftar till att Kemikalieinspektionen ska undersöka möjligheterna till sammarbete i Ukraina inom sitt kompetensområde.

The Swedish Chemicals Agency has submitted a proposal for design support for a possible project in Ukraine. The Ministry of Environmental Protection and Natural Resources of Ukraine has requested support from Sweden on environmental issues. Through this projects the Swedish Chemicals Agency will assess the possibilities for developing a project with support to relevant Ukrainian agencies within the Swedish Chemicals Agency's area of expertise.

The purpose of this design project is to assess the conditions and opportunities for the Swedish Chemicals Agency to develop a long-term cooperation with Ukrainian counterparts within the Swedish Chemicals Agency's areas of competence.
In addition to the originally agreed objective of the design phase support, the aim during the extension period (April to July 2024) is to provide relevant support to Ukraine for key steps in the EU approximation process.

The main result of this preparatory project was the development of a long-term progamme proposal for collaboration with Ukraine on EU accession focused on chemicals management and control. This was successfully delivered by the Swedish Chemicals Agency (KEMI). Sida subsequently appraised support to this long-term programme which was approved in September 2024.
KEMI reviewed documents and provided feedback and expert advice for Ministry of Environment Protection and Natural Resources of Ukraine (MEPR) to prepare for the hearing with the EU Commission in May. This helped MEPR to prepare relevant and more detailed questions to the Commission regarding implementation of the chemicals legislation covered in EU negotiations chapter 27.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
